sources.title: Three Pagodas & Chongsheng Temple: Travel Tips & FAQs 2026
sources.content:
Three Pagodas of Chongsheng Temple - Dali Travel Guide

Overview
The Three Pagodas and Chongsheng Temple represent one of Dali's most iconic landmarks, featuring structures over 1,000 years old alongside a reconstructed temple complex.

Historical Information
The original Chongsheng Temple was destroyed during the Qing Dynasty. The current complex is "a 2005 reconstruction based on archaeological evidence, historical records, and surviving architectural plans." While technically new, it authentically represents architectural styles spanning the Tang through Qing dynasties and remains an active Buddhist worship site.

Key Features & Highlights
- Three Pagodas: Original structures over 1,000 years old; interior access permanently closed decades ago to preserve structural integrity
- Reflection Pond: Popular photography location offering mirror-like views of the pagodas
- Mahavira Hall: Buddhist temple structure
- Wanghai Tower: Viewing platform within the complex

Visitor Practical Information

Hours & Access:
- Opening time: 7:10 AM
- Site contact: +86-872-2666-068

Ticket & Transportation:
- Located 1.5 kilometers from Dali Ancient City
- Electric cart available: CNY 25 (stops at key locations)

Time Required:
- Minimum: 2 hours (pagodas and reflection photography only)
- Recommended: 3-4 hours (thorough exploration)
- Photography enthusiasts: 5+ hours

Accessibility
Partial wheelchair access available; smooth paths at pagoda viewing areas and Reflection Pond, but temple complex involves significant uphill sections with stairs.

Photography Tips
- Arrive at 7:10 AM for calmest Reflection Pond conditions
- Photograph Reflection Pond first (7:10-8:30 AM)
- Return at 4:30 PM for golden hour shots
- Stay through 6:30-7:00 PM for illumination night photography
- Essential gear: wide-angle lens, polarizing filter, extra batteries, tripod

Best Time to Visit
Can visit year-round; summer thunderstorms (June-September) typically clear within 30-45 minutes and create excellent post-rain photography conditions.

Optimal Daily Schedule:
Arrive 7:10 AM, finish by 11:00 AM, then walk to Dali Ancient City for lunch and afternoon exploration.

sources.title: Dali Three Pagodas: Three Pagodas of Chongsheng Temple, Yunnan
sources.content:
Dali Three Pagodas: Three Pagodas of Chongsheng Temple

Located about 1.5 kilometers northwest of Dali Ancient City, these stunning structures stand tall against the backdrop of Cangshan Mountain's Ying Le Peak, overlooking the breathtaking Erhai Lake. They are a must-visit in Dali and the stars of every Dali travel brochure.

Historical Significance
The oldest of the three, the Qianxun Pagoda, boasts an impressive history of over 1200 years, dating back to the latter period of the Nanzhao Kingdom. Behind the Three Pagodas lies the reconstructed Chongsheng Temple, a once-grand sanctuary that, during its heyday, housed over 800 Buddhist chambers and an astonishing 10,000 Buddha statues.

Architectural Details
Qianxun Pagoda is the main pagoda, standing 69.13 meters at the front. Flanking the main pagoda are two smaller north and south pagodas standing about 42.19 meters tall.

Remarkable Features
In 1925, only one in one hundred buildings in Dali survived a devastating earthquake, yet the Three Pagodas remained undamaged. The pagoda's square hollow design with 3.3-meter-thick walls at the base creates a structure that flexes during seismic activity — engineering that predates modern anti-seismic design by a millennium.

Practical Information
Ticket: CNY 121 (includes pagodas + entire temple complex)
Opening Hours: 7:10-19:00 (May-Oct 7); 7:30-18:30 (Oct 8-Apr 30)
Visit Duration: 3-4 hours recommended (minimum 2 hours for basics)
Direct sightseeing buses between Dali Old Town Tourist Center and Chongsheng Three Pagodas are available during 08:30-17:30. It only needs 10 minutes for the drive.
Best Seasons: March to November, especially in spring time.

sources.title: The Three Pagodas of Chongsheng Temple in Dali
sources.content:
The Three Pagodas of Chongsheng Temple in Dali

The Three Pagodas of Chongsheng Temple are among the best-preserved Buddhist structures in China and one of the most iconic landmarks in Yunnan Province. Located about 1.5 km northwest of Dali Old Town at the foot of Cangshan Mountain, the pagodas overlook Erhai Lake.

The main pagoda, Qianxun Pagoda, was built during the Nanzhao Kingdom period (9th century) and stands 69.13 meters tall with 16 tiers. It is a square, hollow brick pagoda in the Tang Dynasty style. The two smaller pagodas, each 42.19 meters tall with 10 tiers, were built during the Dali Kingdom period and feature an octagonal design.

The reconstructed Chongsheng Temple behind the pagodas covers a large area ascending up the mountainside, with multiple halls, courtyards, and Buddhist statues. The temple was rebuilt in 2005 based on historical records.

Key attractions within the complex include the Three Pagodas themselves, the Reflection Pond, Rain Copper Guanyin Hall, and the temple complex ascending to Wanghai Tower at the highest point.

sources.title: Dali Three Pagodas, Yunnan
sources.content:
Dali Three Pagodas

The Three Pagodas of Chongsheng Temple are among the oldest and most well-preserved Buddhist towers in China. Situated at the foot of Yingle Peak of Cangshan Mountain, about 1.5 kilometers northwest of Dali Ancient City, the three pagodas form a symmetrical triangle.

The central pagoda, Qianxun Pagoda, was constructed during the reign of King Quanfengyou of the Nanzhao Kingdom (824-859 AD). Standing at 69.13 meters, it is the tallest pagoda in the group. The two flanking pagodas, each 42.19 meters tall, were built later during the Dali Kingdom period.

In 1978, a major restoration project was undertaken. During the restoration, over 600 Buddhist artifacts were discovered inside the main pagoda, including gold Buddha statues, bronze mirrors, medicinal herbs, and handwritten sutras from the Nanzhao and Dali Kingdom periods.

The Chongsheng Temple behind the pagodas was rebuilt and opened to the public in 2005, ending a long period when the site was described as 'pagodas without a temple.'

sources.title: Three Pagodas - Wikipedia
sources.content:
Three Pagodas

The Three Pagodas (Chinese: 崇圣寺三塔) are an ensemble of three independent pagodas arranged in a symmetrical triangle near the town of Dali, Yunnan province, China. The three pagodas are one of the best-preserved Buddhist structures in China.

The tallest pagoda, known as Qianxun Pagoda, was built during 824-840 AD by the Nanzhao Kingdom. It has 16 tiers and stands 69.13 meters high. The two smaller pagodas were built about a century later during the Dali Kingdom and are each 42.19 meters tall with 10 tiers.

The pagodas are noted for their earthquake resistance. They survived a major earthquake in 1515 and again in 1925 when most buildings in Dali were destroyed.

The site was designated as one of the first group of Major Historical and Cultural Sites Protected at the National Level in 1961.

sources.title: 崇圣寺三塔 - 百度百科
sources.content:
崇圣寺三塔综合信息

基本信息
崇圣寺三塔位于云南省大理古城西北部1.5公里处，是第一批全国重点文物保护单位。该建筑群由一座大塔和两座小塔组成，三塔鼎足而立的独特布局成为大理的标志性景观。

建筑结构

千寻塔（中塔）
这是主要建筑，"高59.4米（台基上皮至塔顶铁圈盘上皮），两层台基高3米，总高62.4米，包括塔刹通高69.13米"。属于方形密檐式空心砖塔，共16层，采用唐代建筑风格。

南北小塔
两座小塔均为八角形密檐式砖塔，各10层，"皆高42.19米"。建筑风格体现宋代特征，相距97米。

历史沿革
三塔建造时间存在多种记载。根据考证，千寻塔最可能建于"南诏王劝丰祐时（824至859年在位）"，而两座小塔则"较中塔为晚，至迟建于大理国初期"。

古籍记载修建三塔"役工匠七百七十万，耗四万余金，历时八年建成"。建造目的除宗教信仰外，还与防治水患有关。

文物发现
1977年维修期间，"于千寻塔塔顶和塔基内清理出南诏、大理时期的佛像、写本佛经等文物600余件"。出土文物包括金质造像、刻字铜片、各式铜镜和珍贵药材。

保护与修缮
国务院于1961年3月将其公布为首批重点文物保护单位。1978至1981年间进行了三年的维修加固工程。2005年4月，崇圣寺完成大规模恢复重建，结束了长期"有塔无寺"的状况。

旅游信息
- 开放时间：8:00-19:00
- 门票价格：75元
- 地点：大理古城北门三文笔村
- 交通：从大理古城北门往北步行约10分钟

周边还有三塔倒影公园，因其清晰倒映三塔的潭水而得名，占地27亩，水面达10多亩。
